items.followUp: State two functions of stems in plants.

rubric.why: Roots take up water and mineral salts from the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.

rubric.why: Roots hold the plant firmly in the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that roots anchor or support the plant in the soil.

modelAnswer: Roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
Roots anchor the plant firmly in the soil.

items.followUp: How much does a normal adult human heart weigh, and what is its approximate size?

rubric.why: The approximate mass of an adult man's heart is 300 g.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the approximate mass.

rubric.why: The heart is approximately the size of the person's closed fist.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for comparing its size with a closed fist.

modelAnswer: The heart of a normal adult man weighs about 300 g.
It is approximately the size of his closed fist.

items.followUp: Define zoology and name two other major divisions of biology.

rubric.why: Biology is the study of life or living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining biology as the study of life or living organisms.

rubric.why: Botany is a major division concerned with plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming botany and/or identifying it as the study of plants.

rubric.why: Zoology is a major division concerned with animals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming zoology and/or identifying it as the study of animals.

rubric.why: Microbiology is a major division concerned with microorganisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming microbiology and/or identifying it as the study of microorganisms.

modelAnswer: Biology is the study of life or living organisms.
Its major divisions include botany, the study of plants;
zoology, the study of animals; and
microbiology, the study of microorganisms.

items.followUp: Name the three types of plastids and state one function of each.

rubric.why: Plastids are membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plastids as membrane-bound organelles in plant cells.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chloroplasts and/or their role in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chromoplasts and/or their pigment-related role.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming leucoplasts and/or their food-storage role.

rubric.why: The three types are chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly listing all three types.

modelAnswer: Plastids are membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
The three types of plastids are chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts.

items.followUp: Give two characteristics of kingdom Monera and two of kingdom Protista.

rubric.why: Monerans are unicellular prokaryotes and lack a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Monerans are unicellular and prokaryotic or lack a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Bacteria, including cyanobacteria, are examples of Monerans.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming bacteria or cyanobacteria as Monerans.

rubric.why: Protists are eukaryotic and mostly unicellular.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that protists are eukaryotic and mostly unicellular.

rubric.why: Many protists live in water; examples include algae and protozoa, and some move using cilia, flagella or pseudopodia.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant characteristic, example or locomotory structure of protists.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Monera consists of unicellular prokaryotes that lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Bacteria, including cyanobacteria, belong to Monera.
Kingdom Protista consists mainly of unicellular eukaryotes with a true nucleus.
Many protists are aquatic; examples include algae and protozoa, and some move by cilia, flagella or pseudopodia.

items.followUp: Write three differences between photosynthesis and respiration.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts containing chlorophyll; respiration mainly occurs in mitochondria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the sites of the two processes.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to produce glucose and oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly giving the materials used and produced in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Respiration uses glucose and oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly giving the materials used and produced in respiration.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis captures light energy and stores it as chemical energy in glucose.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that photosynthesis stores energy.

rubric.why: Respiration breaks down glucose and releases energy for cellular activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that respiration releases energy.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts containing chlorophyll; respiration mainly takes place in mitochondria.
Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and oxygen.
Respiration uses glucose and oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water.
Photosynthesis captures light energy and stores it as chemical energy in glucose.
Respiration breaks down glucose and releases energy for cellular activities.

items.followUp: Compare arteries and veins in terms of direction of blood flow, wall thickness, lumen and valves.

rubric.why: Veins carry blood towards the heart; capillaries connect arterioles and venules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the direction of flow in veins or the connecting role of capillaries.

rubric.why: Capillary walls are only one cell thick, unlike the thicker walls of veins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the very thin, one-cell-thick capillary wall.

rubric.why: Capillaries have a very narrow lumen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for comparing capillaries' narrow lumen with the larger lumen of veins.

rubric.why: Capillaries allow exchange of materials between blood and tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the capillary exchange function.

rubric.why: Veins have valves to prevent backflow; capillaries do not have valves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly comparing valves in veins and capillaries.

modelAnswer: Veins carry blood towards the heart; capillaries connect arterioles to venules.
Veins have relatively thin walls, while capillary walls are only one cell thick.
Veins have a wider lumen; capillaries have a very narrow lumen.
Capillaries allow exchange of materials between the blood and body tissues.
Veins have valves to prevent backflow; capillaries do not have valves.

rubric.why: Biochemistry is a branch of biology.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying biochemistry as a branch of biology.

rubric.why: It studies the chemical composition and chemical processes of living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it studies chemical composition or processes in living organisms.

modelAnswer: Biochemistry is a branch of biology that studies the chemical composition and chemical processes of living organisms.
